note: Hand-curated roads/growth/infrastructure provisos from Part IB of each enacted appropriations act (term-matched candidate sets in provisos/{year}/). Budget provisos are one-year rules enacted inside the annual budget bill; votes attach to the whole appropriations bill (or a named amendment), never to one proviso. Dollar figures are verbatim from the enacted Part IB text. FY 2020-21 had no enacted Part IB (COVID continuing resolution) - stated explicitly per the workflow's none-found rule.

cycles.note: No enacted Part IB this cycle: H5201 died in committee during COVID; the state ran on continuing resolution H3411 plus CARES acts.

provisos.caption: GP: School Construction Development Impact Fee Assessment Prohibition
provisos.why_relevant: Barred local governments from charging development impact fees on new school construction, on pain of losing state aid - a one-year limit on the impact-fee tool that appeared only in this budget and was not renewed.
provisos.verbatim_figure: One-year rule; not renewed in any later budget

provisos.caption: CTC: Increased Funding
provisos.why_relevant: Requires that the extra gas-tax money Act 40 of 2017 sends to County Transportation Committees be spent exclusively on repairs, maintenance, and improvements to the state highway system - a renewed-every-year fix-it-first rule for the county road boards.
provisos.verbatim_figure: First budget in scope with the Act 40 fix-it-first rule

provisos.caption: DOT: Preventative Maintenance Credit
provisos.why_relevant: Authorized SCDOT to transfer part of the gas user fee to cover the Act 40 preventative-maintenance tax credit for drivers. This authorization appeared every enacted budget from FY 2021-22 through FY 2024-25 and stopped appearing in FY 2025-26.

provisos.caption: SR: Homestead Exemption Fund
provisos.why_relevant: A one-time $600 million sweep from the Homestead Exemption Fund whose priority list put $200,000,000 into a CTC Acceleration Fund for county road boards, $100,000,000 into a Bridge Acceleration Fund, and $117,401,000 into a Rural Road Safety Program - the largest one-year roads package in this record.
provisos.verbatim_figure: CTC Acceleration Fund $200,000,000; Bridge Acceleration Fund $100,000,000; Rural Road Safety Program $117,401,000

provisos.caption: DOT: Programmed Project Viewer Dashboard
provisos.why_relevant: Directs SCDOT to upgrade its public Programmed Project Viewer dashboard - project status, forecast versus actual cost, completion dates, and an on-time/on-budget list - with quarterly reports to the budget chairmen. A transparency rule aimed at exactly the project-accountability question citizens raised.

provisos.caption: DOT: Road Buyback Program
provisos.why_relevant: New this year: directs SCDOT to identify state roads that no longer serve a statewide purpose and negotiate transferring them to counties and cities, with buyback funds paying for resurfacing and transition costs - the state shrinking its road inventory by paying locals to take roads back.
